change: Tool-restricted agent definitions and per-skeleton agent types
standfirst: Nine checks, all of them yours — none could be pre-verified, because every one needs a Claude Code restart that no agent in the run can perform. Run Step 0 first. When done—or as soon as something fails—press Copy results as text and paste it into the task.

gate.intro: Run this gate before recording any verdict. Paste the whole block as-is: it runs the same way in cmd.exe and PowerShell.
commands:
git -C "C:/Users/fatbo/OneDrive/Desktop/Claude Testing/orchestrate-skill" branch --show-current
git -C "C:/Users/fatbo/OneDrive/Desktop/Claude Testing/orchestrate-skill" rev-parse HEAD
git -C "C:/Users/fatbo/OneDrive/Desktop/Claude Testing/orchestrate-skill" ls-files .claude/agents/
checks: Branch must be chore/agent-tool-restrictions-ledger. Tested source commit: 168b9d867ff4464092a584e92113c0a03d82de63. A later commit containing only checkpoint artifacts (this page and its sidecar) is allowed.

Canary. The third command must list exactly four files — implementer.md, qa-runner.md, reviewer.md, test-hunter.md. On the base build .claude/agents/ does not exist at all, so it prints nothing. If it prints nothing here you are on the wrong tree — stop and say so rather than recording verdicts. This change bumps no version because nothing in this repo is versioned; the presence of those four files IS the build marker.

sections.title: Restart — do this first
sections.need: The ability to fully quit and reopen Claude Code with this repository as the working directory. No test data, no credentials, no network access.

steps.do: Fully quit and reopen Claude Code, with this repository as the working directory. A new tab or a new session inside the running app is not enough — the process must restart.
steps.pass: The session starts with no error mentioning .claude/agents/.
steps.aside: Runner: human. Every later step depends on this one. Agent definitions are read once at startup, which is the whole reason this checkpoint exists: the session that wrote these files booted before they existed and can never test them.

sections.title: The four roles report their own tools
sections.need: The restarted session from Step 1, and the ability to spawn a sub-agent by subagent_type.

steps.do: Spawn a sub-agent with subagent_type: reviewer and ask it to list every tool it has available.
steps.pass: It reports Read, Glob, Grep and Bash and nothing else — specifically no Write, no Edit, and no mcp__ tool of any kind.
steps.aside: Runner: human. A self-report is a claim, not proof. If it lists a tool you did not expect, that is a fail. And if it declines to use Write rather than reporting Write as unavailable, treat that as a fail too — declining is the honour system this change was built to replace.

steps.do: Spawn a sub-agent with subagent_type: test-hunter and ask the same question.
steps.pass: The same four tools. No Write, no Edit, no mcp__ tool.
steps.aside: Runner: human. Same standard as Step 2 — unavailable, not merely unused.

steps.do: Spawn a sub-agent with subagent_type: implementer and ask the same question.
steps.pass: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash — and no mcp__ tool, no Artifact, no visualize, no Drive, no Gmail.
steps.aside: Runner: human. This role keeps Write and Edit by design. What is being checked is the absence of everything else — the connector and Artifact schemas are the 12–15k per spawn this change removes.

steps.do: Spawn a sub-agent with subagent_type: qa-runner and ask the same question.
steps.pass: The implementer's six tools plus the mcp__Claude_Browser__ browser tools, and no other mcp__ server.
steps.aside: Runner: human. qa-runner keeping Write and Edit is deliberate, not a slip. The request described it as "adds browser tools" right after the read-only pair, but the QA-runner skeleton tells it to write evidence files at each checkpoint — a qa-runner without Write could not produce the evidence a close-out consumes. The reasoning is written into the definition's own body so a later reader does not "correct" it back.

sections.title: End to end — skeleton names a type, the type exists, the type is restricted
sections.need: The restarted session. This is the check the whole change exists for.

steps.do: Open orchestrate/references/subagent-prompts.md and read the line immediately above the Reviewer skeleton's opening fenced block. Then skim the file for the same line above each of the other six skeletons.
steps.pass: Above the Reviewer skeleton: **Spawn with** `subagent_type: reviewer`. The identical form appears above all seven skeletons — Implementer and Fix-up name implementer; Reviewer, Plan pre-flight and Convergence name reviewer; Test hunter names test-hunter; QA runner names qa-runner.
steps.aside: Runner: human. Seven skeletons, four definitions — Plan pre-flight and Convergence share the reviewer's shape (read, judge, write nothing), and Fix-up edits code like an implementer.

steps.do: In the restarted session, spawn the reviewer exactly as that skeleton now instructs — passing the subagent_type the line names — and ask it whether it can edit files.
steps.pass: The spawn succeeds (the type resolves), and the agent reports that Write and Edit are not available to it — not merely that it will not use them.
steps.aside: Runner: human. This is the end-to-end check: the skeleton names a type, the type exists, and the type is restricted. A spawn failure here means the definition's filename and the skeleton's line disagree.

sections.title: What a user without the definitions will read
sections.need: No restart required for these two; they are documentation checks. Step 9 would write into your own home directory if you chose to run its command — you do not have to.

steps.do: Read the new undefined-agent-types bullet in orchestrate/references/protocol.md §Degraded environments.
steps.pass: It says a spawn naming one of these types fails outright and that the orchestrator must substitute the general-purpose agent itself; that the prose read-only rules are then the only enforcement; that the per-spawn saving is forfeited; and it ends in an install action you could actually perform from any repo — copy .claude/agents/*.md into ~/.claude/agents/, then restart. It must not claim anything falls back automatically.
steps.aside: Runner: human. This wording was a blocking review finding. An unknown subagent_type genuinely errors — Agent type 'implementer' not found — so an earlier draft that promised an automatic fallback was wrong, and the draft after that pointed at a README.md which is not shipped with the skill and so resolved to nothing from any other repo. Judge whether the text now helps someone who is not sitting in this clone.

steps.do: Read the new agent-install subsection in README.md. Confirm the command for your platform names a real source path in your clone and your real ~/.claude/agents/ destination. Run it only if you want the agents available in every project.
steps.pass: The subsection states plainly that installing the skill does not install the agents; the command text is correct for your platform and the source path exists; the per-project alternative and the restart requirement are both named; and the fallback sentence says a spawn fails rather than promising an automatic fallback. If you ran the command, the four files are now in ~/.claude/agents/.
steps.aside: Runner: human. This writes into your home directory, not a disposable environment — verifying the text without running it is a valid pass. The trap this subsection exists to close: the skill installs by symlinking orchestrate/ alone, and a skill directory cannot carry agent definitions, so a user who assumes the symlink brought them gets none of the saving.
